strategy_title: Widening BLOCK_N with autotune worsens register pressure and occupancy
strategy_description: Changing BLOCK_N from 16 to 32 in a tall-thin GEMM kernel (M>>N) while adding @triton.autotune over num_warps/num_stages caused registers per thread to jump from 96 to 160, cutting theoretical occupancy from 31.25% to 18.75% and nearly doubling kernel duration (962us → 1610us). Despite the intent to fix 12-way shared memory bank conflicts, the bank conflict rate actually worsened (74.91% → 79.87% wavefront conflict ratio, 12-way → 13.3-way), and executed instructions nearly doubled (154M → 284M). The autotune configs only varied num_warps/num_stages without actually changing BLOCK_N in the kernel signature (BLOCK_N remained a hardcoded constexpr=32), so the tile-widening effect was applied unconditionally while the autotune overhead and register spill dominated.
applicable_when: Never apply this specific pattern. Do not use as a positive template.
do_not_apply_when: Do not unconditionally widen BLOCK_N (or any tile dimension) as a hardcoded constexpr when the kernel is already register-pressure-limited (registers_per_thread >= 80, Block Limit Registers <= 5). Widening a tile dimension increases register usage and can cut occupancy more than it reduces bank conflicts. Do not add @triton.autotune with configs that only vary num_warps/num_stages without including the tile dimension (BLOCK_N) as an autotuned parameter — this applies the tile change unconditionally without finding the optimal tradeoff. Particularly dangerous for tall-thin GEMMs where N is small (N=16) and the output tile BLOCK_M×BLOCK_N already stresses the register file.
framework_notes: In Triton, if BLOCK_N is a hardcoded constexpr inside the kernel body rather than a kernel parameter, @triton.autotune configs cannot vary it. To autotune tile sizes, BLOCK_N must be a kernel parameter (tl.constexpr argument) and included in the configs dict. Autotune over only num_warps/num_stages without tile size variation does not address bank conflict root causes.

The dominant bottleneck is 12-way shared memory bank conflicts (74.91% of wavefronts are conflict wavefronts), causing MIO queue stalls (9.6 cycles) and scoreboard stalls (7.6 cycles) that together account for ~73% of warp stall time. The root cause is the B matrix load pattern: B is stored K-major [K=480, N=16] with stride_bn=480, so the load index `idx_m + 480*idx_n` strides 480 floats (1920 bytes) between consecutive N elements, mapping 16 N-columns to the same 32 shared memory banks repeatedly. The current BLOCK_M=128 forces 96 registers/thread, limiting Block Limit Registers to 5 blocks/SM and theoretical occupancy to 31.25%. Reducing BLOCK_M from 128 to 64 will: (1) cut the accumulator tile from 128x16=2048 to 64x16=1024 elements, reducing register pressure significantly; (2) allow more blocks per SM, increasing theoretical occupancy toward 50-62%; (3) more active warps per scheduler means more latency hiding for the remaining bank-conflict stalls. Prior attempts to fix bank conflicts by widening BLOCK_N (exp_001) caused register explosion (96->160 regs) and 67% slowdown. Prior attempt to reindex B loads (f2cacf29) caused correctness failure. This plan avoids both pitfalls.

applicable_when: The #1 NCU rule (92.64% speedup) is uncoalesced local loads AND stores — this is register spill to local memory. With BLOCK_M=128 and 128 threads/block, the accumulator tile is 128x16=2048 float32 elements. Each thread owns 16 accumulator registers. With maxnreg=64 capping registers, Triton spills the accumulator or loop-carried values to local (L1-backed) memory, causing strided local loads/stores that each use only 1 of 32 bytes per sector — exactly what NCU reports. The fix is twofold: (1) reduce BLOCK_M from 128 to 64, halving the accumulator tile to 64x16=1024 elements so each thread owns only 8 accumulator registers, dramatically reducing register demand; (2) remove the maxnreg=64 cap from all autotune configs so the compiler can allocate registers freely without spilling. The grid MUST be updated from 3920 to 7840 to cover all M=501760 rows. The previous reduce_block_m attempt (item 361a81c4) failed correctness — almost certainly due to forgetting to update the grid from 3920 to 7840 in kernel_function().
